calls.reason: The NANDA report shows custom enterprise tools stalling, and users citing missing memory and adaptation. The same report says users praised ChatGPT and Copilot for immediate usefulness, so the evidence is mixed.

Dated preprints show LLM-based systems keeping lessons from feedback and improving: a frozen-weight agent with memory, SEAL's persistent weight updates, and updates during deployment. That undercuts the categorical 'never'.
CRMArena-Pro, the benchmark he cites, reports about 58% single-turn success, 35% multi-turn and over 83% on workflow execution. That is limited reliability, not agents that don't work 'at all'.
His own estimates of $82B for OpenAI and $77.1B for Anthropic, against the $25B Uber figure, give about 3.3x and 3.1x. Even his generous proxy falls short of 'more than four times'.

Memphis records show heavy power use and real opposition. But a senator reports about 300 xAI staff, a Virginia audit found continuing jobs, and June air tests found no dangerous levels, so the bundled claim is mixed.

Largely rhetoric bundling several assertions. METR found developers were 19% slower with AI, while a Copilot study found lower workload on some tasks, so the evidence is mixed and doesn't cover the financial part.
